backbone: Sieve, transference and Type II bilinear estimates give asymptotics for factorial (joint intensity) statistics of prime factors of p-1; a size-biased argument converts these into the ranked PD(1) law.
quote: Our final passage from interior factor statistics to ranked factors uses the same size-biased approach; that passage is proved explicitly in Section~\ref{pd:section}.

backbone: Decompose the prime sum exactly into Type I and bilinear (Type II) pieces; Voronoi, corrected dispersion and Heath-Brown's cubic large sieve bound each, leaving the explicit main term.
quote: The exact prime decomposition supplies the coefficient classes required by both bilinear branches.

backbone: Reduce to a terminal Q-factorial model with nef dimension three; assuming such data exist, isolate a log canonical component and build a prepared cycle contradicting the companion's cycle obstruction.
quote: To prove Theorem~\ref{thm:main}, it suffices to rule out the following data: an uncountable algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>3$, a terminal $\Q$-factorial projective threefold $X$, an lc pair $(X,B)$,

backbone: Build a curve with prescribed residue data, glue vector-field jets order by order to an analytic surface germ with free tangent sheaf, contract, then algebraize by finite determinacy.
quote: We construct a singular normal affine complex surface whose tangent sheaf is free of rank two.

backbone: Weighted Dolbeault index theory on the cyclic cover yields holomorphic sections whose divisors have compact components; counting b2 rational curves then gives the shell via known criteria.
quote: We construct divisors directly on the infinite cyclic cover of the given surface, and prove that every component is compact.

backbone: Assume the critical exponent inequality fails; extract a differentiability point, build a stationary extremal configuration, and derive incompatible entropy and projection estimates, contradiction; discretize to the maximal bound.
quote: Suppose otherwise. Choose an open interval \(I\) of \(p\)-values, with lower endpoint \(p_{\min}>2\), on which \(h(p,0)>0\).

backbone: Reduce to uniform local tree forms with constants C_N; quadratic-Fourier inverse theorem, curvature localization and side estimates give C_N <= A + c C_N, closing by absorption.
quote: Section~\ref{sec:completion} chooses the parameters and completes the absorption.

backbone: Explicit multiscale strip subset of l2 with bounded doubling; any bi-Lipschitz map to R^k, via near-extremal derivative energy estimates and crossings, yields a packing contradiction; compactness transfers to Banach spaces.
quote: There is a fixed subset $S$ of real $\ell_2$, equipped with its induced Hilbert distance, whose doubling constant is at most $76800$ and which admits no bi-Lipschitz embedding into $\R^k$ for any positive integer $k$, at any finite distortion.

backbone: For each request law, construct an online policy on an evolving separated tree (posterior-driven partitions plus dominated allocation) with potential-function cost bounds; pass to one oblivious policy for all sequences.
quote: For exposition we prove the reusable allocation theorem first, then construct its partition input.

backbone: Inductively construct pairs of strings level by level via signed nested amplification blocks, keeping traces nearly indistinguishable in Hellinger/TV distance at each level, yielding the quasi-polynomial sample lower bound.
quote: The proof is by induction. Section~\ref{sec:initial} supplies level zero. Proposition~\ref{prop:block} constructs the next level, with its observation and likelihood estimates proved in Sections~\ref{sec:layout}--\ref{sec:coefficients}.

backbone: A derivative-times-multiplication rank measure is at most n^{-sqrt n/100} times its maximum for small homogeneous depth-five circuits, but near-maximal for IMM via trace-moment path counting.
quote: Over $\C$, for the partition~\eqref{eq:balanced-schedule}, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for all sufficiently large $n$, \[ R(\IMM_{n,n})\ge D\exp(-C\sqrt n). \]

backbone: Continuous invariant leaves become periodic graphs; Fourier-strip inverses give analytic boundary, a Newton scheme gives a jointly analytic caustic collar, and the companion's collar rigidity forces an ellipse.
quote: Here we establish the additional dynamical and geometric steps needed to apply them to a merely continuous phase foliation. In particular, we construct the physical collar before invoking the companion's ellipse theorem.

backbone: Density-increment iteration on polynomial cells: a progression-free certified set yields a new certificate at threshold (1+eta)a; boundedly many increments give quasipolynomial bounds and summability implies the reciprocal-sum corollary.
quote: then either the hypotheses are impossible or a root slice carries a new certificate at threshold $(1+\eta)a$.

backbone: Necessity: failure of the tensor condition yields an explicit modular colouring. Sufficiency: tensor solutions give equal path endpoints; Hales-Jewett, ultrafilters and compactness force a monochromatic copy.
quote: The $t$ variable positions give squared-distance multiplier $t(1/t)=1$. Compactness supplies a finite ambient dimension for each number of colors.

backbone: Semi-random correspondence colouring: iterated random rounds with entropy-controlled local weight adjustment (vertex splitting to kill triangle mass) and concentration keep invariants until O(Delta/log Delta) colours suffice.
quote: Coloring rounds with dependent entry weights

backbone: Coned random graphs with prescribed types give G; explicit sums cancel in F2 by odd-degree parity; whp no reduced spherical arrangement, giving nonzero factors and aspherical (torsion-free) presentation.
quote: With probability $1-o(1)$, $\Gamma$ admits no reduced spherical arrangement. In particular, for all sufficiently large admissible $n$ there exist graphs of the prescribed types, with girth at least $L$ and the diameter bound of Lemma~\ref{lem:diameter}, admitting no such arrangement.

backbone: Restricted tilting modules give a higher Frobenius functor; iterating it with scalar twists until dimension equality forces exactness lands the category in Ver_{p^n}, yielding the fiber functor.
quote: every finite symmetric tensor category over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$ admits a $k$-linear exact faithful strong symmetric monoidal functor to a finite higher Verlinde category

backbone: Assume escape in both opposite directions with positive probability; regeneration gives integrable radii and opposed tapes; entropy and endpoint-posterior bounds on contacts become incompatible, so coexistence is impossible.
quote: The argument rules out coexistence of escape in opposite directions.

backbone: Tightness plus identification of every subsequential limit: reflection positivity, pin motion and boundary comparison yield harmonic moment identities and a Wick recursion, which determine the Gaussian free field.
quote: The main task is to identify every subsequential limit $H$ of the integer height field.

backbone: Construct a symmetric forcing extension over an auxiliary monoid of diagrams; orbit maps and equivariant quotient bijections give PP and AC_WO, while symmetry blocks a wellorder of A.
quote: We construct a set $A$ of distinct generic subsets of the ground-model $\omega_1$. Symmetry prevents $A$ from being wellordered.

backbone: A kernel element yields a planar disk-and-band surface; a multi-block unitary fixed-space theorem and spectral-phase subadditivity show one nontrivial boundary word is impossible, so the coefficient is trivial.
quote: The upper bound forces the extra term to vanish, so this word is trivial.

backbone: Spatial transfer operator writes partition functions as moments; a coupled purity bootstrap doubles chain length with quadratic defect decay, seeded by certified exact-arithmetic thermal computations at finite length.
quote: This gives a pair of initial purity defects at length $36$; six rounded updates then reach length $2304$.

backbone: Sequential chain: energy bounds give strong locality and a net; annulus estimates integrate modules; fusion positivity and permutation orbifolds unitarize all modules; the CWX functor gives the braided equivalence.
quote: This supplies a starting point for the following sequence.

backbone: Explicit property (T) group with self-embedding; an ultrapower embedding into nuclear B forces, via spectral matching, finitely many approximate representations each with a predecessor, a periodic chain contradiction.
quote: We construct an explicit separable unital full group $C^*$-algebra that admits no unital embedding into $B^\omega$, for any nonzero unital nuclear $C^*$-algebra $B$ and any free ultrafilter $\omega$ on $\mathbb N$.

backbone: Reduce to excluding faithful p-adic actions; a faithful Z_p action would produce sheaf-Witt-group character classes with equal parts in a fixed bounded lattice, contradiction.
quote: Character classes and the contradiction

backbone: Follow a spherical class to its last nonzero homology suspension, a square of a primitive root; fourth powers are excluded and a Steenrod-module obstruction forces Hopf or Kervaire degrees.
quote: The proof is organized around the last nonzero homology suspension of a spherical class.

backbone: Assume a minimal invariant set without fixed point; an adaptive anchor from a compact semigroup and an inductively built tree of maps with separating functionals yield a switching contradiction.
quote: We argue by contradiction for the remainder of the proof and fix $K,T,Y$, and $(z_i)$ as in Lemma~\ref{lem:reduction}.

backbone: A kernel class in pi_9 of stable tubes gives an S^9-family of one-critical-point generating functions realized as an exact embedded Lagrangian; Hamiltonian transport would kill the class, contradiction.
quote: For some sufficiently large even integer $N$, we construct a closed exact smoothly embedded Lagrangian in $T^*(S^9\times S^{N-1})$ that is diffeomorphic to the base but is not Hamiltonian isotopic to the zero section.

backbone: Reduce U(n)-invariant Calabi flow to a scalar fourth-order PDE; a certified self-similar shrinking profile plus an ancient-inverse fixed-point correction gives an exact solution blowing up at T_*.
quote: We construct a smooth K\"ahler metric in the Fubini--Study class of \(\CP^{10}\) whose Calabi flow develops unbounded scalar curvature in finite time.

backbone: Layered cluster expansion over time cells with centering at layer cuts; chronological induction controls remainders through tree counting and dynamical-cutoff estimates, giving L1 convergence of marginals.
quote: We induct on $j$ in chronological order, with $R_k$ already controlling both remainder types whenever $k<j$.

backbone: Compile a Turing machine into a reversible recorder whose affine instructions on rectangles are realized by smooth shear/Hamiltonian flows; the explicit velocity solves forced Navier-Stokes with zero pressure.
quote: A terminating compiler turns a Turing machine and input into a finite program for the force, so a designated particle reaches a fixed region exactly when the machine halts.
